capabilities: Rename top-level frontmatter properties across Markdown files
Update property references in Bases filters, formulas, sorting, grouping, and columns
Preview affected files, locations, and diffs before writing
Create snapshots and undo plans and roll back failed writes
Audit the vault with a read-only Doctor for missing, unused, or drifted properties
disambiguation: Not a general code or text refactoring tool; it only renames top-level frontmatter properties and their references in Bases.
extras: Must currently be built from source or have main.js, manifest.json, and styles.css placed manually in the plugins folder; requires Obsidian 1.9.0 or later. Mobile supports Doctor, scanning, and review only, not writes. Snapshots are stored under .obsidian/plugins/schema-refactor/snapshots/. Runs entirely locally with no account, server, telemetry, or AI service.
motivation: Renaming a property manually risks missing a reference, which can leave a Base incomplete or silently produce wrong results; the author wanted one reviewed workflow for the whole vault.
problem: Renaming a property normally means updating many files by hand, and bulk text replacement is unsafe because the same word can appear in note content, string literals, or unsupported configuration shapes.

relations.evidence: Updates exact property references in supported Obsidian Bases structures.

summary: Vault-wide property renamer that updates frontmatter keys and their Bases references with review, snapshots, rollback, and undo.
